title: Isolation of Polymorphonuclear Leukocytes (Granulocytes)
author: German Alberto
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kggcttw

steps.title: Prepare stock solutions and reagents
steps.instruction: Make all required solutions at the concentrations and densities indicated.

substeps.instruction: OptiPrep 60 % (iodixanol 60 % in water, density 1.320 g/mL ± 0.001, 170 ± 15 mOsm).
HEPES 100 mM (0.238 g/10 mL).
NaOH 1 M (1.999 g/50 mL).
OptiPrep 40 % v/v (density 1.215 g/mL) – mix 4 volumes OptiPrep 60 % with 2 volumes Diluent 1.

Diluent 1: NaCl 0.85 % w/v, 30 mM HEPES‑NaOH, pH 7.4. For 10 mL: 1 mL NaCl 8.5 %, bring to 5 mL with distilled water, add 3 mL HEPES 100 mM, adjust pH with NaOH 1 M, bring to 10 mL (density ≈1.006 g/mL).
Diluent 2: NaCl 0.85 % w/v, 10 mM HEPES‑NaOH, pH 7.4. For 10 mL: 1 mL NaCl 8.5 %, bring to 5 mL water, add 1 mL HEPES 100 mM, adjust pH, bring to 10 mL (density ≈1.006 g/mL).
Leukocyte‑platelet isolation solution (12 % iodixanol, 130 mM NaCl, 1.6 % w/v carboxymethyl cellulose). For 10 mL: 2 mL OptiPrep 60 %, 893 µL NaCl 8.5 %, 0.16 g carboxymethyl cellulose.
Density solution 1.077 g/mL: for 10 mL mix 3.396 mL OptiPrep 40 % + 6.604 mL Diluent 2.
Density solution 1.095 g/mL: for 10 mL mix 4.26 mL OptiPrep 40 % + 5.74 mL Diluent 2.
Lysis solution: NaCl 1.8 % w/v, 20 mM HEPES‑NaOH, pH 7.4.

steps.title: Collect fresh blood with anticoagulant
steps.instruction: Draw fresh blood (use within 6 h) into tubes containing EDTA to a final concentration of 2 mM (or another anticoagulant) and gently homogenize.

steps.title: Layer blood onto isolation solution and sediment
steps.instruction: In a new 15 mL tube add 1 mL leukocyte‑platelet isolation solution, gently overlay 3 mL whole blood, and let erythrocytes sediment through the density barrier for 1.5–2 h at room temperature without centrifugation; the upper layer becomes leukocyte‑rich plasma.

steps.title: Add density gradients and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Create a stepwise density gradient beneath the plasma layer and centrifuge.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the 3 mL leukocyte‑rich plasma to a fresh 15 mL conical tube.
Using a narrow‑bore Pasteur pipette, slowly add 3 mL density solution 1.077 g/mL beneath the plasma.
Gently add 3–4 mL density solution 1.095 g/mL along the tube wall, avoiding mixing.
Centrifuge at 800 g for 25 min at 18–22 °C with no brake.

steps.title: Harvest PBMC and PMN fractions, wash PMNs
steps.instruction: Separate the cell layers, dilute and wash the PMNs.

substeps.instruction: Using a Pasteur pipette or a needle, aspirate the two bands separating the three interfaces into separate tubes: the upper band (PBMCs) and the lower band (PMNs).
Dilute the PMN suspension with an equal volume of Diluent 2.
Centrifuge at 250 g for 10 min.
Resuspend the PMN pellet in pre‑warmed appropriate medium (medium placed at 37 °C for at least 10 min); handle gently to minimise activation.

steps.title: Optional erythrocyte lysis and final resuspension
steps.instruction: Remove residual erythrocytes if needed and prepare the final cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the PMN pellet in 3 mL lysis solution and incubate at 37 °C for 7 min; OR resuspend in 3 mL ice‑cold distilled water, wait 30 s, then add 3 mL of NaCl 1.8 % / 20 mM HEPES‑NaOH pH 7.4.
Centrifuge at 250 g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the pellet in appropriate medium.
Count cells with a hemocytometer or Neubauer chamber, assess viability with trypan blue, and optionally verify purity by flow cytometry (side‑scatter/forward‑scatter).

steps.title: Count cells in each fraction
steps.instruction: Measure cell numbers in the leukocyte‑rich plasma, PBMC, and PMN fractions by hemocytometry and record the results.
